title: DNS transmitted over TCP is framed with a length of two bytes
summary: Each DNS message over TCP begins with a two-byte length in network byte order. The length counts the message bytes, excluding the prefix.
detail: A TCP payload may contain only half a DNS message, or may contain multiple messages, and should be divided by this prefix on the ordered byte stream.
boundary: The UDP DNS message itself does not have this TCP length field.
relevance: Explain the truncation or concatenation that occurs when DNS records are split directly by capture lines.
